description: Sensitive-content classifier: a small linear head over the SigLIP 2 embedding already computed for every image. Gates what may enter an automated album, a shared reel, or a contact sheet sent to the frontier model.

normalisation.calibration_note: Sigmoid output is already a probability, so no rescale. The threshold is 0.3 rather than 0.5 on purpose and is the one number in this file that is a policy decision rather than a technical one -- see notes.

license.training_data:
SELECTED, NOT YET BUILT. docs/safety-classifier-decision.md surveyed thirteen candidates and rejected all twelve third-party options on provenance rather than on licence: there is no off-the-shelf open NSFW classifier with documented, rights-cleared training data. So the head is a construction, not a download -- a 1152x3 linear map initialised from SigLIP 2's own text tower over a prompt bank committed at packages/safety-gate/memory_engine_safety/prompts.json, then per-class Platt-calibrated on an internally assembled corpus whose every image carries a recorded source, licence and collection date.

Image provenance chain: WebLI, and nothing else -- the corpus already assessed and accepted for siglip2-so400m-384. ZERO third-party NSFW images and ZERO third-party NSFW weights enter this entry, ever. Third-party NSFW models may be used offline inside packages/eval-harness for rank-agreement sanity checks and hard-case mining only; they may never be a label source, because that would launder their provenance into ours and make this a distillation of a corpus the audit rejected.

Measured explicit recall on photographic pornography is UNKNOWN and recorded as a gap, not a pass: no permissively licensed, model-released explicit corpus is obtainable, so §6.3(a) validates that class against boundary material only until a licensed evaluation set is commissioned.
license.note:
STILL BLOCKING, AND FOR A NARROWER REASON THAN BEFORE. The model is chosen (docs/safety-classifier-decision.md §6) and the head, its calibration and the gate wiring exist in packages/safety-gate. What does not exist is a weights file: the head is a matrix over the SigLIP 2 embedding, and SigLIP 2 has no ONNX export in this registry yet (issue #79). Nothing can be fitted, hashed or measured until that lands.

So the state is unchanged where it counts. weights.blake3 is null, rollout.state is placeholder, license.verified is false, and blocks_commercial_release stays true -- which means the load gate refuses this entry in RELEASE mode for three independent reasons and refuses it in EVERY mode for being a placeholder. The safety gate reads that refusal as `model_unavailable`, which is `indeterminate`, which blocks the publication. That is the designed behaviour and not a bug to route around: an unaudited safety classifier is worse than none, because it produces a number that looks like a safety guarantee.

Promotion requires all of: the SigLIP 2 ONNX export (#79); the head fitted and hashed; the eval gate in decision §7 passed with per-slice reporting and the bias gate; and license.verified true with a date and a human's name.

notes:
PLACEHOLDER FOR THE SHAPE, STILL -- but for a different reason than before. The head is now chosen rather than unselected (docs/safety-classifier-decision.md §6), and it is ours: a 1152x3 linear map over the SigLIP 2 embedding, initialised from SigLIP 2's own text tower. What is missing is a weights file, because SigLIP 2 has no ONNX export in this registry yet (issue #79) and there is nothing to fit a head against. Chosen-but-unbuilt is a placeholder, and calling it anything else would let it load.

THE CLASS AXIS IS NOW PINNED, AND THAT IS THE REAL FIX IN THIS DIFF. `sensitive_logits` is shape [-1, 3] and until now nothing anywhere said which index was which class. Transpose two columns and every breastfeeding photograph classifies as explicit: the scores stay in [0,1], the 0.3 threshold still fires, the clearance manifest still validates, and no test in the repository fails. `outputs[0].class_order` states the mapping, models/schema/model-config.schema.json refuses a safety_classifier entry that omits or reorders it, and contracts/schemas/safety-clearance.schema.json pins the same three strings as a const on ClassifierPin.class_order -- so a config edited here cannot produce a manifest that validates there.

THREE CLASSES, NOT ONE FLAG. The head emits explicit / suggestive / medical-or-artistic rather than a single 'nsfw' bit, because collapsing them is what produces the two classic failures: a breastfeeding photo or a post-surgery record treated as pornography, and a bikini holiday photo treated as safe for a shared reel. A family library contains all three and the right handling differs for each.

THE THRESHOLD IS ASYMMETRIC ON PURPOSE. 0.3, not 0.5. A false positive quietly omits one photo from an automated album, which the user can override. A false negative puts sensitive content into a printed book, a shared reel, or a contact sheet uploaded to a frontier model -- and the last of those is irreversible the moment it leaves the device. Those costs are not symmetric, so the threshold should not be either.

EXCLUSION IS NOT DELETION. A flagged photo stays in the library, stays searchable by its owner, and is only withheld from automated and shared output. The classifier decides what the system publishes on the user's behalf; it never decides what the user may keep.

Runs on the embedding, so it costs nothing beyond the SigLIP pass that already happened -- which is the reason it can run on everything rather than on a sample, and coverage is what a safety gate needs most.

BATCHING (issue #31): DEMOTED TO 1, UNVERIFIED. This entry declared supported=true, max_batch=256, dynamic_axes=true. weights.blake3 is null, so the ONNX graph it names has never been produced or hashed, let alone had its input shape read -- the claim was an assumption wearing the clothes of a measurement, which is the same defect issue #31 found in the YuNet entry. Restore it by running onnxruntime.InferenceSession(...).get_inputs()[0].shape against the pinned checkpoint and recording that in batching.verified_against. Declining to batch costs throughput and nothing else.
